title: Cashier POS
headline: Take the order. Keep the context.
description: A menu-led cashier workspace for selecting products and sending confirmed orders into kitchen preparation.

steps.title: Select from the menu
steps.description: Browse categories and add the requested products to the cart.

steps.title: Add the service context
steps.description: Attach a table and guest details where the order needs them.

steps.title: Send it to preparation
steps.description: Cashier submission confirms the order and creates its kitchen ticket.

boundary: The capture shows menu selection with an empty cart. Tax, payment, receipt and offline workflows require separate acceptance; no payment terminal or offline reliability is promised.

faqs.question: When is a cashier order confirmed?
faqs.answer: Submitting it confirms the order and creates its kitchen ticket.

faqs.question: Does this screen promise tax or payment behavior?
faqs.answer: No. Tax, payment, receipts and offline operation require separate verification.

title: Kitchen display
headline: A clear next action for every ticket.
description: See incoming orders and coordinate preparation through new, in-progress, ready and completed ticket states.

steps.title: Receive the confirmed order
steps.description: An open kitchen display receives a ticket for the confirmed order.

steps.title: Move preparation forward
steps.description: Bump the ticket to in progress, then ready, as work advances.

steps.title: Review and recall
steps.description: Find completed tickets and recall one when the team needs to revisit it.

boundary: Kitchen completion is separate from delivery and payment. The demonstrated handoff is not a guarantee of delivery under every network condition or of multi-station routing.

faqs.question: When does a ticket appear?
faqs.answer: After a cashier order is submitted or staff confirm an online order.

faqs.question: Does a completed ticket mean the order was paid?
faqs.answer: No. Kitchen preparation, fulfillment and payment are separate states.

title: Online ordering
headline: From your guest’s menu to your team’s queue.
description: Guests browse a restaurant storefront, review a cash-on-delivery checkout and receive an order confirmation.

steps.title: Choose from the restaurant menu
steps.description: The guest adds a product and reviews the cart.

steps.title: Send a cash order
steps.description: Checkout creates a pending order and returns its confirmation.

steps.title: Let staff confirm
steps.description: Staff confirmation sends the order into the kitchen preparation queue.

boundary: The demonstrated flow uses the configured demo storefront and cash on delivery. Online card processing and instant availability of newly registered public hostnames are not promised.

faqs.question: Can guests pay online by card?
faqs.answer: This verified flow supports cash on delivery. Online card processing is not available in this demonstrated flow.

faqs.question: When does an online order reach the kitchen?
faqs.answer: After restaurant staff confirm the pending guest order.

title: Storefront customization
headline: Your colors. A menu that feels like yours.
description: Use the theme editor to adjust colors, save the configuration, preview it and activate a restaurant theme.

steps.title: Start with a theme
steps.description: Review a restaurant theme or duplicate it into your own configuration.

steps.title: Make a considered change
steps.description: Adjust a color and inspect the preview; the editor also surfaces contrast feedback.

steps.title: Save and activate
steps.description: Saved configuration persists after reload and can be exposed by the restaurant’s public theme endpoint.

boundary: This is storefront configuration, not arbitrary page building. Editor previews can use sample content. Public hostname and TLS setup is a separate onboarding requirement; instant publishing is not promised.

faqs.question: What can the editor change?
faqs.answer: The verified workflow edits storefront theme colors, saves the configuration and previews it.

faqs.question: Does saving instantly provision a public domain?
faqs.answer: No. Public hostname and TLS setup is a separate onboarding step.

title: Inventory
headline: See the stock effect of a confirmed order.
description: Connect tracked product quantities with order confirmation and eligible unfulfilled cancellations.

steps.title: Start with tracked stock
steps.description: The demonstrated product began with 20 available units.

steps.title: Confirm one item
steps.description: Confirmation reserved one unit and changed the available quantity to 19.

steps.title: Release an eligible cancellation
steps.description: Cancelling the unfulfilled order restored the quantity to 20.

boundary: This example does not establish ingredient recipes, purchasing, historical valuation or automatic physical returns. Refunding money is different from returning stock.

faqs.question: What happens when one tracked unit is confirmed?
faqs.answer: The verified example moves available stock from 20 units to 19.

faqs.question: What happens after an eligible unfulfilled cancellation?
faqs.answer: The reserved unit is released and stock returns to 20. A money refund or physical return is separate.

title: Staff records
headline: Keep attendance and leave decisions organized.
description: Maintain employee information, attendance records and leave requests within the restaurant workspace.

steps.title: Keep employee information
steps.description: Create and review the employee’s record.

steps.title: Record attendance
steps.description: Record clock-in and maintain clock-out information through attendance editing.

steps.title: Review a leave request
steps.description: Record approval or rejection and revisit the request’s resulting state.

boundary: These are demonstrated record-keeping actions. Statutory payroll, automatic working-hour accuracy, country-specific HR compliance and performance-review workflows are not advertised.

faqs.question: Which staff workflows are demonstrated?
faqs.answer: Employee records, attendance records and leave decisions.

faqs.question: Is statutory payroll or HR compliance included?
faqs.answer: Those capabilities have not been verified and are not claimed here.

title: Operational overview
headline: Know what needs your attention next.
description: Review recent orders, pending work, basic workspace counts and subscription status in an operational overview.

steps.title: Review recent work
steps.description: Use the latest loaded orders and pending-order count as a starting point.

steps.title: Check the workspace
steps.description: Review available product, team and table information for your current restaurant.

steps.title: Understand the data context
steps.description: The overview identifies unavailable sources and shows when data was loaded.

boundary: Recent paid revenue is based on the latest loaded orders, not a complete accounting period. Financial statements, forecast accuracy and consolidated multi-location reporting are outside this demonstrated scope.

faqs.question: What does the operational overview summarize?
faqs.answer: Recent loaded orders, pending work, workspace counts and subscription status.

faqs.question: Is this a financial statement?
faqs.answer: No. Recent paid revenue is not a complete accounting period or consolidated report.
